summary: The household's frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: none beat most random baskets drawn from the same list, and simply holding every name equally did better than the index fund and every rule. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. Today's calls are four neutral, low-conviction watches on names in the rule's pretend record; nothing here is expected to beat the index. Real money stays on the household's horizon plan.
eli5: The brain looked at old races and saw that picking the fastest runners did no better than picking names from a hat. So it is only watching a few stocks with pretend money, like a game of make-believe shop. The family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket every week.
letter: Dear family, here is our note for the week. First, real money. Nothing changes. Long-term money gets its weekly buy of the whole-market fund, money needed within a few years keeps its safe part, and money needed within a year stays safe. One red or green day is no reason to rush anything. Second, the pretend game. We tested every stock-picking rule we wrote down in advance against baskets drawn at random from the same list, and every one was rejected. Owning all the names equally did better than any rule and better than the index fund. Our weekly bet has been scored only once and lost; luck alone wins about half the weeks, so a few weeks tell us nothing. Our stock calls stay neutral and low. Third, the lesson. Picking the front runners felt sensible and did not pay here. A good orchard is tended for years, not judged by one morning's fruit. Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then on paper for at least half a year, ahead of the core. Until then we keep it simple. With care, the brain.
